kjv: a target of brass between his shoulders
mine: a bronze javelin slung between his shoulders
note: Hebrew kidon is a javelin or curved sword (the War Scroll uses it of a sword); "target" (a small shield) is a guess, and the KJV itself renders kidon "spear" in v. 45 margin and "shield" in v. 45 text.
Hebrew ma'gal (from 'agol, "round") means the circular camp or wagon ring, not a dug trench.

kjv: left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage
mine: left his baggage in the care of the keeper of the baggage
note: Hebrew kelim means equipment or baggage; "carriage" in 1611 meant what is carried, but now suggests a vehicle.
Hebrew roa' levavekha is "wickedness of heart"; "naughtiness" now sounds like childish misbehaviour.

mine: Was it not just a word?
note: Hebrew halo' davar hu' most naturally means "it was only a word / I was only talking"; the KJV takes davar as "reason, cause", making David justify his intervention.
Hebrew kidon, the same weapon as in v. 6, is an offensive weapon (javelin or sword) listed with sword and spear; the KJV's "shield" breaks the series of offensive arms.
Hebrew chalele pelishtim are the slain (chalal, "pierced, fatally wounded"); also MT "until you come to Gai" is read by the KJV as "the valley" (gay'), while the Septuagint reads Gath.
